messages:
sam: heads up — seeing a burst of dcgm exporter ECC/XID alerts across eu-west GPUs since ~08:22 UTC. ~40 short spikes that mostly self-resolve within 3–6m. graphs: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abcd/dcgm-gpu?var-region=eu-west
priya: ugh, saw that feed. are they correlated to a single kernel/driver bump or network flakiness?
sam: no obvious infra deploys at that time, no kernel churn. noise looks card-local — multiple cards on the same host but not all hosts.
mateo: can we avoid mass node drains? last time autoscaler started evicting and it killed many jobs. propose an aggregation + short-suppression rule: only page if per-card XID rate is sustained for 10m and occurs on >1 successive 10m bucket. sketch below.
priya: show the sketch pls
sam: ```yaml
groups:
- name: dcgm-noise-aggregation
  rules:
  - record: job:dcgm_xid_per_card:increase5m
    expr: sum by (instance,gpu_index) (increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_total[5m]))
  - alert: DcgmPersistentXidPerCard
    expr: job:dcgm_xid_per_card:increase5m > 0 and increase(job:dcgm_xid_per_card:increase5m[10m]) > 2
    for: 10m
    labels:
      severity: page
      route: primary-oncall
    annotations:
      summary: "Persistent XID spikes on {{ $labels.instance }}/gpu{{ $labels.gpu_index }}"
      runbook: "https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-xid-triage"
```
lina: reasonable. couple notes: 1) keep a counter-style recording rule so we can still surface cumulative resets (do not entirely hide), 2) add label escalation=manual if node moves into drain path so automation can skip initial suppression.
mateo: +1 for the `escalation=manual` label. otherwise this rule might mask a real failing card that needs replacement. also prefer `for: 10m` so we give transient stuff a chance.
priya: ops question — do we want to change scrape_interval for dcgm-exporter? higher resolution helped in past, but increases prometheus load.
lina: let's avoid changing scrape frequency for prod. aggregation + recording rules are cheaper and reversible. we can test shorter scrape in a staging pool.
ops-bot: ops-bot: opened PR #3425 adding the recording rule and alert to the staging rules file (refs: gitlab.com/redwood/monitoring/-/merge_requests/3425).
oncall-bot: oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-054 created for noisy GPU alerts; assigned to @sam.
sam: can someone deploy PR to staging and then run a sim to validate alert suppression? I can run the smoke test and confirm no drain triggers.
priya: deploying to staging now. will watch for 30m.
sam: test sim (local):
```bash
# simulate 5 xid increments on gpu0 (staging exporter supports /inject for test)
for i in {1..5}; do
  curl -s -X POST http://staging-exporter:9000/metrics/inject -d 'dcgm_gpu_xid_total{gpu_index=\"0\",instance=\"staging-node-21\"} 1'
done
```
mateo: note — if we see repeated suppressed alerts, add a small metric that counts suppressed_alerts_total{instance,gpu_index} so SRE can monitor suppression rate.
lina: agreed. add metric + grafana panel showing suppressed vs paged alerts.
sam: thanks. i'll update the oncall runbook with the new detection thresholds and a small play for manual replacement steps (plug -> reseat -> replace). :thumbsup:
priya: watching now, will report back in ~30m.
